newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Four die in petrol bomb attack on Belgian cafe.
newsitem.headline: Four die in petrol bomb attack on Belgian cafe.

text.p: Four Belgians died in a blazing Brussels apartment building on Monday after a petrol bomb was thrown into a ground floor cafe, police said.
Eight people were interrogated by public prosecutors in connection with the fire-bombing which killed three middle-aged men and a woman, a police spokesman said.
Two of the victims had not yet been identified, he added.
Police were detaining five of the eight people interrogated, the spokesman said. No charges had been brought so far. "They are being confronted with witnesses," he added.
The detained men were apprehended after witnesses saw a white car racing away from the scene of the explosion in the Brussels commune of Molenbeek, an area with a large immigrant population.
"We have no clear picture of the motives...but revenge cannot be ruled out," the spokesman said. The petrol bomb attack occurred in the early hours of Monday after the cafe closed.
"There was a loud bang, the sound of breaking glass and screeching tyres," one witness said. The explosion was heard at a nearby police station.
Belgian media reported there had been a fight between the cafe's Moroccan owner and the building's Belgian tenants. The La Batavia cafe had been the scene of gambling, it said.
"There have been problems, conflicts in this building, but nothing of the kind to justify a scandalous and violent act of this kind," Molenbeek mayor Philippe Moureaux said.
A woman and her four children had a narrow escape. Just thirty seconds after fire brigade rescuers reached them, the room they had been in burst into flames.
